mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility is declining week-on-week (11.3→7.1 over four weeks), indicating people are spending less time at home. This sustained outflow from residential space drives compensatory increases in retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks as displaced home time reallocates to commerce and leisure.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 11.3 to 7.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL continues to decline below 5.0 in week t+1w.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -20.3 to -14.6 over four weeks, a 5.7-point recovery. This workplace return signal will propagate to retail-and-recreation within one week as commuters resume incidental shopping and leisure activities during and after work trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -20.3 to -14.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not sustain improvement above -15.0 in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC declines in week t+1w.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized near -20.3 (from -24.6 four weeks prior), signaling restored confidence in public transport. This confidence recovery interacts with WORKPLACES recovery to unlock retail-and-recreation visits concentrated around transit hubs over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves >3 points AND WORKPLACES improves >3 points in same week
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES reverses by >2 points in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC does not rise above -18.0 in week t+2w.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated from -32.1 to -27.9 over four weeks, a 4.2-point improvement but still deeply suppressed. This modest parks recovery is insufficient to sustain outdoor leisure substitution, forcing consumers back into enclosed retail-and-recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS improves above -20.0 in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC declines below -22.0 in week t+2w.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized at -10.1 (from -11.0 four weeks prior), indicating essential shopping routines are normalized. This normalization of essential-goods trips interacts with the RETAIL_REC baseline decline to signal that discretionary retail suppression is ending, producing retail-and-recreation recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM volatility exceeds ±2.0 points in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC remains below -20.0 for two consecutive weeks starting t+1w.

failure_condition: Any of the three proxies reverses by >3 points in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC does not improve above -18.0 by week t+4w.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -24.6 to -20.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT reverses by >1.5 points in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC does not improve in week t+1w.

This reallocation of time from home to work signals behavioral shift toward pre-restriction patterns, which will cascade into retail-and-recreation recovery over two weeks as work-trip incidental shopping resumes.

fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 4.2 points over four weeks
